text:
jess: Hey team — our CI started failing with 401 invalid_api_key when calling /v1/embeddings from linux runners. Works locally. Key was copied from the dashboard and stored in secrets.json. Anyone seen this?

support-bot: New support ticket #123456 created and assigned to support.

marta: @jess can you paste the exact curl you run (masked key is fine) and the raw response body?

jess: Sure — here's what the runner shows:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
{"error":{"message":"Invalid API key","type":"invalid_api_key"}}
```

samir: Is $REDWOOD_KEY populated from secrets.json? Can you check raw bytes, e.g. `echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY" | xxd -p | sed 's/../& /g'` on the runner?

jess: Ran that on the failing runner, pasted output below (masked part shown):
```
73 6b 2d 61 62 63 5c 72 37 38 39 30 2d 78 79 7a
```

marta: That hex shows `5c 72` which is the ASCII for the two characters `\` and `r` (i.e. a backslash followed by the letter r). That means the secret contains a literal backslash+`r` sequence in the token (e.g. `sk-abc\r7890...`) instead of an actual CR character — or more likely it was exported/stored as an escaped JSON string.

ops_sre: Right — some JSON serializers or copy-export flows produce escaped sequences (`\r`, `\n`) in the JSON string. When that string is written verbatim into an env var, the literal backslash and letter become part of the key. Redwood treats that as a different token so you get 401.

ops_sre: Quick repro/fix commands you can run on the runner:
1) show bytes: `echo -n "$RAW" | xxd -p`
2) unescape with printf: `UNESCAPED=$(printf "%b" "$RAW")` then `echo -n "$UNESCAPED" | xxd -p` (should remove 5c 72)
3) or with python: `python -c 'import sys; print(sys.argv[1].encode("utf-8").decode("unicode_escape"))' "$RAW"`

jess: Did `UNESCAPED=$(printf "%b" "$RAW")` and re-ran curl — got HTTP/1.1 200 and embeddings back. Rotating the key now and will update CI secret with the unescaped value.

marta: Thanks — marking this solved. We'll add a KB note: "If you paste keys from JSON exports, unescape `\n`/`\r` sequences before storing in CI secrets." :white_check_mark:

jess: Added a preflight check to our deploy pipeline: `echo -n $KEY | xxd -p | grep -q 5c && echo 'possible-escaped-seq-in-key'` so deploys fail loudly if these bytes show up.

samir: Nice. Also added a one-liner to the support playbook to ask for `echo -n $KEY | xxd -p` output early in triage for 401s.

marta: Closing thread — reach out if you hit any rotation/rollback issues.
